subject: Chemistry
title: Why Alcohol Makes You Drunk
description: A 60-second lesson on Why Alcohol Makes You Drunk.

hook.text: Ethanol is a tiny molecule that crosses the blood-brain barrier in minutes and slows your neurons.

buildup.text: It enhances the effect of GABA, an inhibitory neurotransmitter. Your brain literally slows down.

discovery.text: It also blocks glutamate receptors—your brain's main excitatory signal. Double the slowdown.

twist.text: Your liver breaks ethanol into acetaldehyde—a toxic molecule that causes hangovers and nausea.

climax.text: Genetic variations in alcohol-processing enzymes explain why some people flush red after one drink.

punchline.text: Ethanol boosts the brakes and cuts the gas. That's being drunk.

quiz.question: How does ethanol affect the brain?
options: It enhances inhibitory signals and blocks excitatory ones
It speeds up all neural activity
It directly kills brain cells on contact

details.summary: Ethanol is a small molecule that crosses the blood-brain barrier easily and enhances the effect of GABA, an inhibitory neurotransmitter, while reducing the effect of glutamate, an excitatory one. This chemical imbalance slows neural signaling, impairing coordination, judgment, and reaction time.
details.whyItMatters: Understanding alcohol's chemistry explains tolerance, addiction, and why it affects judgment before motor skills. It is the most widely used psychoactive substance and a leading cause of preventable death.
takeaways: Ethanol enhances inhibitory GABA and suppresses excitatory glutamate
The liver metabolizes ethanol to acetaldehyde, then to acetic acid
Acetaldehyde is toxic and causes many hangover symptoms

faq.question: Why do people feel more social after one drink but lose coordination after several?
faq.answer: Low doses of alcohol primarily affect the prefrontal cortex, reducing social inhibition while motor areas are less impacted. Higher doses progressively impair the cerebellum (coordination), hippocampus (memory), and eventually the brainstem (breathing and heart rate).

faq.question: Why do some people get red-faced when they drink alcohol?
faq.answer: About 36 percent of East Asian people carry a variant of the ALDH2 enzyme that processes acetaldehyde poorly. Acetaldehyde accumulates, causing facial flushing, nausea, and rapid heartbeat..
